title: Future technology: a balanced argument
prompt: Write three paragraphs discussing whether future technology will give people more free time. Present possible benefits, counterarguments and your own conclusion. Use examples and future forms.
checks: Use an example marker such as for instance.
End with a supported personal view.

title: Report a small survey
prompt: Invent a small fictional survey about study habits. State the number of respondents, give three percentages and describe the pattern. Clearly label the data as fictional and avoid claiming the survey proves a cause.
checks: Use expressions such as the graph shows.

title: A story checked against evidence
prompt: Write a short fictional coincidence story, then a factual summary of what its invented records actually support. Use both, neither and each accurately. Separate missing evidence from evidence that disproves a claim.
checks: Distinguish a claim from its evidence.
Use both, neither or each correctly.

title: A concise personal statement
prompt: Choose an imaginary job and write a personal statement for a fictional applicant. Match specific skills to the job rather than listing unsupported claims. Use concise descriptive phrases.
checks: Use a phrase such as a keen eye for detail.
Keep the statement focused and concise.

title: A fictional remote company
prompt: Write a company profile for an imaginary team that works remotely three days a week. Explain its work, communication methods and possible benefits. Use two opening participle phrases and two cause-and-effect expressions.
checks: Make the participle phrase refer to the main-clause subject.

title: Summarize a topic
prompt: Write a short summary of how an imaginary maker turned a hobby into a small project. Give the main idea and important stages without adding unsupported details. Use one cleft sentence for emphasis.

title: Summarize a viewpoint
prompt: Write a short summary of an imaginary writer’s argument about preserving a local language. State the writer’s main claim, supporting reasons and conclusion. Distinguish the writer’s view from an established fact.
checks: Attribute the opinion to the writer.
Use a structure such as while some say … the author feels.
Do not add a new argument as if it were in the text.

title: Turn a short article into slides
prompt: Create four short text slides for a fictional presentation about organizing study time: a title slide and three tips. Give each tip a short heading and brief supporting points. Avoid copying long paragraphs onto a slide.
checks: Give one main point per slide.

title: Explain a community project
prompt: Write a paragraph about an imaginary project that gives a community access to a shared resource. Define the problem, explain what the project does and describe the intended result. Keep facts and hoped-for outcomes distinct.
checks: Use a phrase such as by definition or fundamentally.
Link the project to its intended outcome.

title: Summarize a discussion formally
prompt: Invent three short viewpoints about sharing tools in a neighborhood. Write a formal summary that identifies agreements, benefits and limitations. Attribute each opinion and use formal linking expressions.
checks: Use a phrase such as with respect to.

title: An identity for a fictional team
prompt: Write an opinion essay proposing a name, mascot and colors for an imaginary local sports team. Give examples supporting your choices. Describe color associations as your interpretation rather than universal facts.
checks: Distinguish your associations from other people’s preferences.

title: A concise character arc
prompt: Invent a short fictional story and write a clear plot summary. Show the character’s starting situation, key challenge and change. Edit long sentences so the sequence is easy to follow.
